steps.query: Red-team read of the gtn pages for gtn rollforward.

candidate.text: Merck's US sales before discounts rose only about 2% in 2025 while net US sales rose 13%: the US discount provision fell from $13.3B to $10.0B, so the gross-to-net rate dropped to about 21% from 29% (2024) and 30% (2023). The cut in Januvia's list price explains the drop mechanically, not stronger pricing, and $249M of 2025 revenue was a release of prior-year rebate accruals, up from $139M in 2024 and $70M in 2023.

steps.query: Red-team read of the footnotes pages for royalty footnote.

candidate.text: Merck's 2.5% royalty on every dollar of Keytruda and Keytruda Qlex sales, paid to BMS and Ono under the PD-1 patent settlement, ends after December 31, 2026, so roughly $0.8B a year of cost of sales disappears in 2027 (about $0.54B to $0.79B net of Winrevair royalty growth and a possible European Qlex royalty). It is a one-year step, not a run-rate: the Keytruda compound patent ends in December 2028, and Lynparza generics could start taking part of it back as early as late 2027 (earliest approval date only; see MRK-nugget-012).

steps.query: Red-team read of the footnotes pages for litigation footnote.

candidate.text: Keytruda Qlex, Merck's defense against 2028 to 2029 IV biosimilars, is enjoined in Germany by Halozyme (appeal hearing Nov 19, 2026), faces a Dutch counterclaim covering seven more European countries with a ruling due about end October 2026, and Merck warns it may owe 'additional royalties' on Qlex. The risk is European: in the US the PTAB has found every challenged claim unpatentable in four decisions, and Halozyme consented to revocation in the UK. Qlex sold $463M in Q2 2026, of which only $68M was outside the US.
